key_insight: Non-binary detector error models preserve circuit-fault correlations and represent any Pauli channel exactly, while yielding smaller graphs and better belief-propagation decoding performance in the reported evaluations.
engineering_relevance: Tanner graphs with 4–5× fewer edges can reduce decoder hardware demands, while BP with OSD achieved up to 9.4× CPU speedup.
method: Model each circuit fault location as one random variable over its original error alphabet.
Use split–merge–regroup to combine error components with identical detector and observable flips.
Decode using belief propagation with one scalar message per edge, optionally followed by OSD.
evidence_signal: Numerical evaluations on surface, color, and bivariate bicycle codes report better BP performance with and without OSD, 4–5× fewer graph edges, and up to 9.4× faster BP with OSD on CPU.
watch_item: The reported speedup is CPU-based; hardware benefits require validation, and equivalence to binary models is proven only for factorizing channels under degenerate quantum MAP decoding.
